title: Continental Forge leadership gallery: neutralise a mixed-light headshot batch to one house look against an in-frame grey card, knock the six execs onto the brand-grey band, and cut a responsive set
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com corporate-website retouch open call ('professionally enhance a complete set of images for our corporate website'; 'correct lighting imbalances and exposure issues'; 'create a consistent visual style across all website images'; 'prepare images for desktop, tablet, and mobile responsiveness'; 'showcase our facilities, operations, equipment and people'; 'maintain a natural and realistic appearance'). The real posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL precision-machining firm, Continental Forge Group, and the vague open call is fixed into a runnable, gradeable batch: EIGHT team headshots shot across different rooms and days under deliberately different light (warm boardroom tungsten, cool north-window daylight, green shop-office fluorescent, mixed, amber lamp, open-shade cool), each with a neutral grey/white balance reference card placed in frame so 'consistent visual style' becomes a measurable neutralisation target instead of an eyeball claim. The brief's literal 'remove distractions / put people on a clean backdrop' is honoured the ONLY connector-legal way for the six leadership heroes — a subject knockout onto a flat brand-grey ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) — NOT AI object removal, NOT select-subject->invert->solid-fill (that anti-pattern is the planted trap). Two floor portraits deliberately stay in their working environment (the triage). Brand-grey hex (#5E5E5E), responsive sizes (1920/1024/640) and the grey-card tolerance are pinned because the source gives none. No layout composition, no generative fill, no text-to-image is claimed.
one_line_ask: Take eight client-shot corporate headshots photographed under six different lightings (each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralise and grade every one to one consistent Continental Forge house look measured against the card, route the six leadership heroes onto the flat brand-grey web band while leaving the two shop-floor portraits in their environment, protect skin tone under the grade, then cut a responsive set for the lead hero.
full_brief:
Continental Forge Group is a precision metal-forging and CNC-machining firm rebuilding its 'Our Team' and 'Leadership' web pages. Our internal photographer shot everyone over three days in whatever room was free, so the raw set does not match: the CEO was lit by warm boardroom downlights and runs hot and slightly over; the plant director was shot against a cool north window and reads blue and a touch dark; the operations manager sat under old green shop-office fluorescents; the QA lead is a mixed window-plus-tube split; the engineering lead is under an amber desk lamp; the HR director is in cool open shade; and two of the crew were caught at their stations on the floor. Because we knew the light was a mess, the photographer clipped a neutral grey balance card (an 18 percent grey patch beside a white patch) into every frame.

What we need: make the whole set read as ONE deliberately-designed gallery, true-to-skin and premium, not eight mismatched snapshots. Use the grey card in each frame as your ground truth — every image must be neutralised so that card reads truly neutral (no residual warm, blue or green cast) and so the card's mid-grey sits at the same brightness across all eight, tolerance about three levels of channel spread on the card and the set's mid-grey within roughly four levels of a common target. Then carry ONE shared house look across all eight — a restrained, slightly warm-highlight / cool-neutral-shadow corporate tone with modest contrast and clarity and a gentle vibrance lift — so contrast and colour feel identical head to head. The catch our last freelancer failed: do not let the vibrance push turn faces orange or plasticky. Skin has to stay natural while the rest of the frame gets the lift.

Second, the two pages treat people differently and you must route each shot to the right treatment. The SIX leaders (CEO, plant director, operations manager, QA lead, engineering lead, HR director) go on the Leadership band, which sits on our flat brand-grey backdrop — brand grey is exactly #5E5E5E — so each leader must be lifted cleanly off their messy original room and set on that solid grey ground with hair and shoulders looking natural, no halo, no cardboard cutout. The TWO shop-floor portraits are meant to show the plant in action and MUST keep their real working background — do not knock those out. Getting that routing wrong ruins the page and nobody notices until it is live.

Finally cut the responsive set for the lead hero (the CEO) off the finished brand-grey master at desktop 1920px, tablet 1024px and mobile 640px wide, subject-centred and web-light, sRGB. Deliver: the eight graded masters as a contact set our marketing lead can eyeball against the card, the six leaders on the #5E5E5E band at 800x800, the CEO responsive trio, and a short written note listing the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each image and the skin protection you applied, so we can confirm they were actually matched to the card and not just eyeballed.

inputs.name: hero_ceo_boardroom_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate half-body headshot of a 55-year-old female CEO (fictional, Marisol Vance) in a charcoal blazer, seated in a boardroom lit by warm tungsten ceiling downlights. Slightly overexposed and clearly WARM/amber colour cast, flat-to-normal contrast. A neutral grey balance card (an 18 percent grey patch next to a small white patch) is clipped to her lanyard and clearly visible in the lower frame. Real skin pores, fine lines, a few flyaway hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #1 and the responsive lead. Deliberately WARM + slightly over so its corrective white-balance/exposure move differs from every other frame. The in-frame grey card is the neutralisation ground truth. Warm boardroom skin must not go orange under the shared vibrance lift.

inputs.name: hero_plant_director_window_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate headshot of a 48-year-old male plant director (fictional, Devon Achebe) in a navy quarter-zip, shot against a large cool north-facing window. Clearly COOL/blue colour cast and slightly UNDER-exposed, flat contrast. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey patch beside a white patch) sits propped at the frame edge, clearly visible. Real skin texture with pores, individual hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #2. Cool + under: the OPPOSITE corrective direction to the CEO, so a single shared white balance across the batch cannot possibly neutralise both — this is the identical-params trap. Grey card is the target.

inputs.name: hero_ops_manager_fluoro_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate headshot of a 44-year-old female operations manager (fictional, Priya Nandakumar) in a rust cardigan, lit by old overhead GREEN fluorescent shop-office tubes. Distinct green/magenta-deficient colour cast, normal exposure, slightly dull. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey and white patches) is clipped visibly at the lower edge of frame. Real skin pores and fine flyaway hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #3. Green fluorescent cast needs a TINT (green->magenta) correction, not a temperature correction — a different axis from the warm/cool frames, forcing per-image reasoning rather than one slider.

inputs.name: hero_qa_lead_mixed_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate headshot of a 39-year-old male QA lead (fictional, Tomas Reinholt) in a light grey shirt, lit by a MIX of cool window light on one side and warm tube light on the other so the cast is split and uneven across the face. Normal exposure, flat contrast. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey plus white patch) is visible propped in frame. Real skin texture, pores, a few stray hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #4. Split/mixed cast is the hardest to neutralise to the card; the agent must average toward the card's neutral rather than fully killing one side.

inputs.name: hero_engineering_lead_amber_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate headshot of a 51-year-old male engineering lead (fictional, Yusuf Bello) in a black polo, lit by a single warm AMBER desk lamp, strongly warm and a little contrasty with a soft shadow side. Normal-to-slightly-bright exposure. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey and white patches) is clipped in view at the frame edge. Real skin pores, fine lines, flyaway hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #5. Strong amber cast, deeper skin tone: its skin-protection HSL trim must differ from the lighter-skinned frames, so 'protect skin' is a per-subject decision, not one global setting.

inputs.name: hero_hr_director_openshade_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera corporate headshot of a 46-year-old female HR director (fictional, Clara Whitfield) in a plum blouse, shot in cool OPEN SHADE outside a roller door, cool-blue and slightly flat, normal exposure. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey patch beside a white patch) is visible at the lower frame. Real skin pores, fine hairs, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Leadership hero #6. Cool open-shade, but a subtly different blue than the north-window frame, so its corrective is close-but-not-equal — the agent cannot copy one fix across the two cool frames.

inputs.name: floor_portrait_machinist_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera environmental portrait of a machinist (fictional crew, not named) standing at a CNC lathe on a busy shop floor, mixed warm-cool factory light, slightly cool and flat. Real working background clearly visible: parts bins, coolant lines, a control panel. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey and white patch) is clipped to the machine guard in view. Real skin, natural hands, safety glasses. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Triage member #1: MUST stay environmental (the working background is the point). If the agent knocks this onto brand grey it has misread the routing. Still graded to the card + house look like the rest.

inputs.name: floor_portrait_technicians_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Straight-out-of-camera environmental portrait of two technicians (fictional crew, not named) at an inspection bench on the shop floor, overhead fluorescent plus window, slightly green and normal exposure. Real working background: gauges, a whiteboard, tool racks. A neutral grey balance card (18 percent grey plus white patch) is propped on the bench in view. Real skin texture, natural hands. 3:2, 4000x2667px, un-retouched, documentary, NOT glossy, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Triage member #2: also stays environmental, and it is a TWO-person frame so select_subject behaves differently than on the solo heroes; graded to the card + house look but never knocked out.

outputs.name: team_gallery_graded_x8
outputs.spec: The eight retouched masters as one matched contact set: each neutralised to its in-frame grey card (card reads neutral, no residual warm/blue/green cast; card mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target across the set; ~3-level channel spread tolerance on the card), then the single shared Continental Forge house look applied (warm-highlight / cool-neutral-shadow, modest contrast + clarity, gentle vibrance) with skin protected per subject so faces stay natural. Full-res PNG (~4000x2667). The six leaders and the two floor portraits are all present and visibly consistent head-to-head.

outputs.name: leadership_band_x6
outputs.spec: The six leaders (CEO, plant director, ops manager, QA lead, engineering lead, HR director) each lifted off their original messy room and set on the flat brand-grey ground exactly #5E5E5E via a subject knockout (image_remove_background with backgroundColor), hair and shoulders clean with no halo, then cropped subject-centred to 800x800, sRGB. The two floor portraits are deliberately NOT in this deliverable.

outputs.name: hero_ceo_responsive_set
outputs.spec: The lead hero (CEO) responsive trio cut from her finished brand-grey master: desktop 1920px, tablet 1024px, mobile 640px wide, subject-centred, web-light, sRGB. Same graded/knocked-out master, three sizes.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per image: the corrective white-balance move made to hit the card (temperature and tint direction/magnitude), the exposure delta, and the skin-protection HSL trim applied, plus a one-line confirmation that each frame's grey card reads neutral and lands on the common mid-grey target. This makes 'matched to the card' verifiable rather than asserted.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_ceo_boardroom_raw.jpg, hero_plant_director_window_raw.jpg, hero_ops_manager_fluoro_raw.jpg, hero_qa_lead_mixed_raw.jpg, hero_engineering_lead_amber_raw.jpg, hero_hr_director_openshade_raw.jpg, floor_portrait_machinist_raw.jpg, floor_portrait_technicians_raw.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Ingest all eight client raw headshots into the working project so every downstream edit runs against real asset references. Plumbing, not difficulty.

CEO (warm boardroom, slightly over): read the in-frame grey card and COOL the temperature + pull exposure down until the card is neutral and its mid-grey hits the common set target. WB/exposure values are computed to THIS frame's cast; the shared house-look tonal shape (contrast/clarity/highlight-warm/shadow-cool/vibrance) is applied in the same call as the batch-wide constants. Report the temp/tint/exposure move for the params note.
Select the CEO so skin can be protected without touching the background; person-only selection is exactly what select_subject supports.

Masked skin protection: inside the subject mask, trim the orange/red hue-band saturation and nudge its luminance so the shared vibrance lift does not push warm-lit skin orange. Only masked recolor path available (adjust_hsl accepts a mask). Produces the CEO graded master.

Plant director (cool north window, slightly under): WARM the temperature and LIFT exposure to the card — the opposite corrective to the CEO, proving a single shared WB cannot serve both. Apply the same shared house-look constants. Report the move.
Select the plant director for skin-safe grading.
Masked skin protection tuned to this subject's complexion (different from the CEO). Produces the plant director graded master.

Masked skin protection; green-cast frames especially need the residual green pulled out of skin. Produces the ops manager graded master.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining. All eight raws enter once via asset_add_file(1). Each image runs a three-step per-frame sub-chain: image_apply_adjustments neutralises THAT frame's specific cast to its in-frame grey card and lays the shared house-look constants (the WB/exposure inputs differ per frame, the tonal shape is constant); image_select_subject builds a person mask; image_adjust_hsl consumes [neutral, subject_mask] for skin protection, emitting that frame's graded master (steps 2-4 CEO, 5-7 plant, 8-10 ops, 11-13 QA, 14-16 eng, 17-19 HR, 20-22 machinist, 23-25 technicians). The six leadership masters then fan into image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#5E5E5E}) knockouts (26-31); the two floor masters are deliberately NOT knocked out (the triage). Each knockout feeds an 800x800 band crop (32-37 => leadership_band_x6), and the CEO knockout additionally fans into the responsive trio (38-40 => hero_ceo_responsive_set). Every step after the single ingest consumes a named prior output via inputs_from; team_gallery_graded_x8 is the eight graded masters, and the params note reports the per-frame corrective moves.
difficulty_rationale: Depth, not plumbing: 40 connector calls but only ONE upload and zero folder/copy padding — 39 of 40 are real edits. Six distinct Adobe tools over a batch of eight assets shot under six different lightings. The hardness is (a) cross-asset consistency to a MEASURABLE target: every frame must be neutralised to its own in-frame grey card (neutral card, common mid-grey, ~3-level spread / ~4-level mid-grey tolerance) while the corrective differs per frame — warm/over vs cool/under vs green-tint vs split vs strong-amber vs cool-shade, on different colour axes (temperature vs tint), so the reasoning is genuinely per-image; (b) an agent-authored house look built from primitives (image_apply_adjustments split-tone + contrast/clarity/vibrance) applied as shared constants, NOT a preset, NOT auto_tone; (c) masked skin protection tuned per complexion so the vibrance lift never turns faces orange; (d) triage — six heroes must be knocked onto the exact brand-grey ground while two floor portraits must stay environmental, a routing the brief states as a goal and does not spell out per-image; (e) the knockout must use the connector-legal remove_background({backgroundColor}) path rather than the flat-plate select->invert->fill anti-pattern; (f) the responsive fan-out. The agent must REPORT its final per-image WB/exposure/skin moves, making 'matched' checkable. All connector work is [C] headless-confirmed.
hardness_rationale: Failure gate: the agent can trip and be caught, because every frame carries an in-frame neutral grey card and the acceptance test is that each card reads truly neutral (no residual warm/blue/green cast, ~3-level channel spread) with the card mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target across all eight, and the agent must REPORT the per-image temperature/tint/exposure move — a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the batch leaves the cool frames blue and the green frame green and fails the gate. Human-hard elements: (1) cross-asset neutralisation of eight differently-lit headshots to a shared measurable card target on differing correction axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs split-cast compromise), which a novice cannot match by eye; (2) triage of two superficially identical inputs into DIFFERENT correct treatments — six leaders knocked onto the #5E5E5E brand ground, two floor portraits kept environmental — where a wrong route is invisible until the page is live; plus masked per-complexion skin protection so the grade never oranges skin. The trap: the brief's 'put our leaders on the brand-grey backdrop' invites the naive select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area chain, which looks right but solid-fills a flat plate with a hard halo and wrecks hair edges (and is the documented anti-pattern); the connector-legal path is image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#5E5E5E}). Measurable acceptance criterion: every grey card neutral within ~3 levels of channel spread and its mid-grey within ~4 levels of the common set target; the six knockouts on exactly #5E5E5E; leadership crops 800x800 and the CEO responsive trio at 1920/1024/640px, sRGB; and a per-image parameter report so 'matched to the card' is verifiable rather than asserted.
